title: Extension Allowance Decision Table — Builder Extended Rate Lock
content:
An extension that uses up the extension allowance of a Builder Extended Rate Lock carries a higher extension fee percent.

**Rule.** An extension after which both the term's maximum increments and the term's maximum total extension days are used adds 0.0625 percentage points to the extension fee percent; one after which either the maximum increments or the maximum total extension days, but not both, are used adds 0.03125 percentage points; any other extension adds nothing. The points are added to the extension fee percent before it is applied to the loan amount on the lock.

After the extension, the increments used are the extensions used on the lock record, and the extension days used are the extension days already carried by extension fee charges on the lock ledger plus the days of the extension being priced.

## Allowance by term

| Lock term | Maximum increments | Maximum total extension days |
|---|---|---|
| 60-Day Standard Lock | 3 | 21 |
| 90-Day Lock | 3 | 21 |
| 120-Day Extended Lock | 2 | 30 |
| 180-Day Extended Lock | 2 | 30 |
| 270-Day Build Lock | 2 | 60 |
| 360-Day Build Lock | 1 | 30 |

## Decision table

| Maximum increments used after the extension | Maximum total days used after the extension | Added |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | 0.0625 |
| Yes | No | 0.03125 |
| No | Yes | 0.03125 |
| No | No | nothing |

## Cases (hypothetical histories)

- A 270-Day Build Lock after an extension of 2 increments of 30 days: 2 increments and 60 days used, both maxima reached, 0.0625 added.
- A 360-Day Build Lock after one 30-day increment: 1 increment and 30 days, both reached, 0.0625 added.
- A 90-Day Lock after 2 increments of 7 days: 2 of 3 increments and 14 of 21 days, neither reached, nothing added.
